goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
goldens.reasoning: The golden comment's main point is that mixing float with flexbox causes layout problems. C1 makes the same point: floats, including float: left on .topic-avatar, are ignored once .small-action becomes a flex container. However, C1 is about .small-action, not the header .panel and noscript header issue the golden comment also describes, so this is only a partial match.

goldens.comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate says that -ms-align-items is not a real property.

goldens.comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate covers the box-ordinal-group values needing to start at 1.

candidates: app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss:264 - Making `.small-action` a flex container stops its `float: right` button from aligning right.. `.small-action` is now `display: flex`. Browsers ignore `float` on flex items, so the `float: right` on `.small-action` `button` (and the `float: left` on `.topic-avatar`) no longer has any effect. Nothing in this rule pushes the button to the right edge: `.small-action-desc` doesn't grow and the button has no `margin-left: auto`. So small-action posts that show an edit/delete button will place it right after the description text instead of at the right edge. I couldn't check the markup order, so I don't know exactly where the button lands. Fix: add `margin-left: auto` to the button (or `flex: 1` to `.small-action-desc`), and remove the floats that no longer do anything.
